ChatGPT said:

Yes — the error is clear. Your game code is mostly fine. The problem is specifically with the Tkinter image object.

Why you're getting this error

You are running the code in Jupyter/Anaconda Notebook (Cell In[3]). When Tkinter is repeatedly run in notebook cells, the PhotoImage can belong to a different Tkinter interpreter than the root window. That causes:

TclError: image "pyimage2" doesn't exist

Also, your image is named sudokuimage.jpg, which is fine as long as the file is actually in the same folder as the notebook/script.

Best solution for your project

Since this is a beginner project, I recommend running it as a normal .py file, not inside a Jupyter cell.

Create:

Games_Project/
│
├── main.py
└── sudokuimage.jpg

Then run:

Bash
python main.py

There is also a small improvement I recommend: use Image.Resampling.LANCZOS when resizing the background.

Your background section should be:

Python
import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
import random

# =========================================================
# MAIN WINDOW
# =========================================================

root = tk.Tk()
root.title("🎮 Game Collection")
root.geometry("700x700")
root.resizable(False, False)

# Load background image
background_image = Image.open("sudokuimage.jpg")

# Resize background
background_image = background_image.resize(
    (700, 700),
    Image.Resampling.LANCZOS
)

# Convert image for Tkinter
background_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(
    background_image,
    master=root
)

# Create background
background_label = tk.Label(
    root,
    image=background_photo
)

background_label.place(
    x=0,
    y=0,
    width=700,
    height=700
)

# Keep a reference to the image
root.background_photo = background_photo

The important part is:

Python
background_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(
    background_image,
    master=root
)

and:

Python
root.background_photo = background_photo

These help ensure the image belongs to the correct Tkinter window and isn't garbage-collected.

One more problem in your code

You currently have:

Python
BG_COLOR = "#01ff07"

That's very bright green. Then your subtitle and footer use it:

Python
bg=BG_COLOR

This can make the background image look strange because the labels cover parts of it with bright green.

Change:

Python
BG_COLOR = "#01ff07"

to:

Python
BG_COLOR = "#000000"

However, because you are using a background image, I recommend making the labels slightly transparent-looking isn't directly supported by standard Tkinter. A simple dark background is better.

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import messagebox
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
import random


# =========================================================
# MAIN WINDOW
# =========================================================

root = tk.Tk()
root.title("🎮 Game Collection")
root.geometry("700x700")
root.resizable(False, False)


# =========================================================
# BACKGROUND IMAGE
# =========================================================

try:
    background_image = Image.open("sudokuimage.jpg")

    background_image = background_image.resize(
        (700, 700),
        Image.Resampling.LANCZOS
    )

    background_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(
        background_image,
        master=root
    )

    background_label = tk.Label(
        root,
        image=background_photo
    )

    background_label.place(
        x=0,
        y=0,
        width=700,
        height=700
    )

    # Keep image in memory
    root.background_photo = background_photo

except FileNotFoundError:

    root.configure(bg="#17202A")

    messagebox.showwarning(
        "Background Image",
        "sudokuimage.jpg was not found.\n"
        "The program will run without the background image."
    )


# =========================================================
# COLORS
# =========================================================

BG_COLOR = "#17202A"
TITLE_COLOR = "#FFD700"


# =========================================================
# TIC TAC TOE
# =========================================================

def tic_tac_toe():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("❌⭕ Tic-Tac-Toe")
    game.geometry("500x600")
    game.resizable(False, False)
    game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="❌⭕ TIC-TAC-TOE",
        font=("Arial", 25, "bold"),
        fg="#F7DC6F",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=20)

    board = [""] * 9

    buttons = []

    player = ["X"]

    turn_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Player X's Turn",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    turn_label.pack(pady=10)

    def reset_game():

        for i in range(9):

            board[i] = ""

            buttons[i].config(
                text="",
                bg="#2C3E50"
            )

        player[0] = "X"

        turn_label.config(
            text="Player X's Turn"
        )

    def check_winner():

        combinations = [
            (0, 1, 2),
            (3, 4, 5),
            (6, 7, 8),
            (0, 3, 6),
            (1, 4, 7),
            (2, 5, 8),
            (0, 4, 8),
            (2, 4, 6)
        ]

        for a, b, c in combinations:

            if (
                board[a] != ""
                and board[a] == board[b]
                and board[b] == board[c]
            ):

                buttons[a].config(bg="#27AE60")
                buttons[b].config(bg="#27AE60")
                buttons[c].config(bg="#27AE60")

                messagebox.showinfo(
                    "Winner",
                    "🎉 Player "
                    + board[a]
                    + " Wins!"
                )

                reset_game()

                return True

        if "" not in board:

            messagebox.showinfo(
                "Game Over",
                "🤝 It's a Draw!"
            )

            reset_game()

            return True

        return False

    def play(index):

        if board[index] != "":
            return

        board[index] = player[0]

        buttons[index].config(
            text=player[0]
        )

        if player[0] == "X":

            buttons[index].config(
                fg="#E74C3C"
            )

        else:

            buttons[index].config(
                fg="#3498DB"
            )

        if check_winner():
            return

        if player[0] == "X":

            player[0] = "O"

        else:

            player[0] = "X"

        turn_label.config(
            text="Player "
            + player[0]
            + "'s Turn"
        )

    frame = tk.Frame(
        game,
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    frame.pack()

    for i in range(9):

        button = tk.Button(
            frame,
            text="",
            font=("Arial", 30, "bold"),
            width=5,
            height=2,
            bg="#2C3E50",
            fg="white",
            activebackground="#566573",
            command=lambda i=i: play(i)
        )

        button.grid(
            row=i // 3,
            column=i % 3,
            padx=5,
            pady=5
        )

        buttons.append(button)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🔄 NEW GAME",
        font=("Arial", 14, "bold"),
        bg="#E67E22",
        fg="white",
        width=18,
        command=reset_game
    ).pack(pady=25)

# ROCK PAPER SCISSORS
# =========================================================

def rock_paper_scissors():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("✊ Rock Paper Scissors")
    game.geometry("500x650")
    game.resizable(False, False)
    game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="✊✋✌️ ROCK PAPER SCISSORS",
        font=("Arial", 21, "bold"),
        fg="#F7DC6F",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=25)

    result = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Choose your move!",
        font=("Arial", 20, "bold"),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    result.pack(pady=20)

    computer_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Computer: ❓",
        font=("Arial", 16),
        fg="#AED6F1",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    computer_label.pack(pady=10)

    score = {
        "player": 0,
        "computer": 0,
        "draw": 0
    }

    score_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="You: 0     Computer: 0     Draw: 0",
        font=("Arial", 15, "bold"),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    score_label.pack(pady=20)

    choices = [
        "Rock",
        "Paper",
        "Scissors"
    ]

    def play(player_choice):

        computer_choice = random.choice(
            choices
        )

        computer_label.config(
            text="Computer: "
            + computer_choice
        )

        if player_choice == computer_choice:

            score["draw"] += 1

            result.config(
                text="🤝 DRAW!",
                fg="#F1C40F"
            )

        elif (
            player_choice == "Rock"
            and computer_choice == "Scissors"
        ) or (
            player_choice == "Paper"
            and computer_choice == "Rock"
        ) or (
            player_choice == "Scissors"
            and computer_choice == "Paper"
        ):

            score["player"] += 1

            result.config(
                text="🎉 YOU WIN!",
                fg="#2ECC71"
            )

        else:

            score["computer"] += 1

            result.config(
                text="😔 COMPUTER WINS!",
                fg="#E74C3C"
            )

        score_label.config(
            text=
            "You: "
            + str(score["player"])
            + "     Computer: "
            + str(score["computer"])
            + "     Draw: "
            + str(score["draw"])
        )

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="✊ ROCK",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        bg="#E74C3C",
        fg="white",
        width=20,
        command=lambda: play("Rock")
    ).pack(pady=10)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="✋ PAPER",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        bg="#3498DB",
        fg="white",
        width=20,
        command=lambda: play("Paper")
    ).pack(pady=10)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="✌️ SCISSORS",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        bg="#9B59B6",
        fg="white",
        width=20,
        command=lambda: play("Scissors")
    ).pack(pady=10)


# =========================================================
# NUMBER GUESSING
# =========================================================

def number_guessing():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("🔢 Number Guessing")
    game.geometry("500x550")
    game.resizable(False, False)
    game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

    number = [random.randint(1, 100)]

    attempts = [0]

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="🔢 NUMBER GUESSING",
        font=("Arial", 25, "bold"),
        fg="#F7DC6F",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=30)

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Guess a number between 1 and 100",
        font=("Arial", 15),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=10)

    entry = tk.Entry(
        game,
        font=("Arial", 20),
        justify="center",
        width=10
    )

    entry.pack(pady=20)

    result = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Good luck! 🎯",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        fg="#AED6F1",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    result.pack(pady=15)

    def reset():

        number[0] = random.randint(
            1,
            100
        )

        attempts[0] = 0

        entry.delete(
            0,
            tk.END
        )

        result.config(
            text="New number generated! 🎯"
        )

    def guess_number():

        try:

            guess = int(
                entry.get()
            )

        except ValueError:

            result.config(
                text="Please enter a number!"
            )

            return

        attempts[0] += 1

        if guess < number[0]:

            result.config(
                text="⬆️ Too Low!"
            )

        elif guess > number[0]:

            result.config(
                text="⬇️ Too High!"
            )

        else:

            messagebox.showinfo(
                "Congratulations!",
                "🎉 Correct!\n"
                "Attempts: "
                + str(attempts[0])
            )

            reset()

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🎯 GUESS",
        font=("Arial", 15, "bold"),
        bg="#27AE60",
        fg="white",
        width=15,
        command=guess_number
    ).pack(pady=10)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🔄 NEW GAME",
        font=("Arial", 14),
        bg="#E67E22",
        fg="white",
        width=15,
        command=reset
    ).pack(pady=10)

def snake_and_ladder():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("🎲 Snake and Ladder")
    game.geometry("650x750")
    game.resizable(False, False)
    game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

    position = [1]

    snakes = {
        99: 54,
        95: 75,
        92: 73,
        64: 60,
        62: 19,
        56: 53,
        49: 11,
        47: 26
    }

    ladders = {
        4: 25,
        9: 31,
        21: 42,
        28: 55,
        36: 44,
        51: 67,
        71: 91,
        80: 100
    }

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="🎲 SNAKE & LADDER",
        font=("Arial", 25, "bold"),
        fg="#F7DC6F",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=15)

    position_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Position: 1",
        font=("Arial", 16, "bold"),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    position_label.pack(pady=5)

    dice_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="🎲",
        font=("Arial", 35),
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    dice_label.pack()

    board = tk.Frame(
        game,
        bg="black"
    )

    board.pack(pady=10)

    cells = {}

    for row in range(10):

        for col in range(10):

            number = (
                (9 - row) * 10
                + col
                + 1
            )

            cell = tk.Label(
                board,
                text=str(number),
                width=5,
                height=2,
                font=("Arial", 9, "bold"),
                bg="#F8F9F9",
                relief="solid",
                borderwidth=1
            )

            cell.grid(
                row=row,
                column=col
            )

            cells[number] = cell

    def update_board():

        for number in cells:

            cells[number].config(
                text=str(number),
                bg="#F8F9F9"
            )

        for start in ladders:

            cells[start].config(
                text="🪜 "
                + str(start),
                bg="#ABEBC6"
            )

        for start in snakes:

            cells[start].config(
                text="🐍 "
                + str(start),
                bg="#F5B7B1"
            )

        cells[position[0]].config(
            text="🔴 "
            + str(position[0]),
            bg="#F9E79F"
        )

    def roll_dice():

        dice = random.randint(
            1,
            6
        )

        dice_label.config(
            text="🎲 "
            + str(dice)
        )

        if position[0] + dice <= 100:

            position[0] += dice

        if position[0] in ladders:

            position[0] = ladders[
                position[0]
            ]

        elif position[0] in snakes:

            position[0] = snakes[
                position[0]
            ]

        position_label.config(
            text="Position: "
            + str(position[0])
        )

        update_board()

        if position[0] == 100:

            messagebox.showinfo(
                "Winner",
                "🎉 Congratulations!\n"
                "You reached 100!"
            )

    def reset():

        position[0] = 1

        position_label.config(
            text="Position: 1"
        )

        dice_label.config(
            text="🎲"
        )

        update_board()

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🎲 ROLL DICE",
        font=("Arial", 15, "bold"),
        bg="#3498DB",
        fg="white",
        width=18,
        command=roll_dice
    ).pack(pady=8)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🔄 NEW GAME",
        font=("Arial", 14),
        bg="#E67E22",
        fg="white",
        width=18,
        command=reset
    ).pack()

    update_board()

def hangman():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("🪢 Hangman")
    game.geometry("550x650")
    game.resizable(False, False)
    game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

    words = [
        "python",
        "computer",
        "program",
        "school",
        "game",
        "keyboard",
        "teacher"
    ]

    word = [
        random.choice(words)
    ]

    guessed = []

    attempts = [6]

    tk.Label(
        game,
        text="🪢 HANGMAN",
        font=("Arial", 28, "bold"),
        fg="#F7DC6F",
        bg="#1B2631"
    ).pack(pady=25)

    word_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="",
        font=("Arial", 28, "bold"),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    word_label.pack(pady=25)

    attempts_label = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Attempts: 6",
        font=("Arial", 16),
        fg="#AED6F1",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    attempts_label.pack(pady=10)

    entry = tk.Entry(
        game,
        font=("Arial", 20),
        justify="center",
        width=5
    )

    entry.pack(pady=15)

    result = tk.Label(
        game,
        text="Guess a letter!",
        font=("Arial", 16),
        fg="white",
        bg="#1B2631"
    )

    result.pack(pady=10)

    def update_word():

        display = ""

        for letter in word[0]:

            if letter in guessed:

                display += letter + " "

            else:

                display += "_ "

        word_label.config(
            text=display
        )

    def reset():

        word[0] = random.choice(
            words
        )

        guessed.clear()

        attempts[0] = 6

        attempts_label.config(
            text="Attempts: 6"
        )

        result.config(
            text="Guess a letter!"
        )

        entry.delete(
            0,
            tk.END
        )

        update_word()

    def guess_letter():

        letter = entry.get().lower()

        entry.delete(
            0,
            tk.END
        )

        if (
            len(letter) != 1
            or not letter.isalpha()
        ):

            result.config(
                text="Enter one letter!"
            )

            return

        if letter in guessed:

            result.config(
                text="Already guessed!"
            )

            return

        guessed.append(letter)

        if letter in word[0]:

            result.config(
                text="✅ Correct!"
            )

        else:

            attempts[0] -= 1

            result.config(
                text="❌ Wrong!"
            )

        attempts_label.config(
            text="Attempts: "
            + str(attempts[0])
        )

        update_word()

        if all(
            letter in guessed
            for letter in word[0]
        ):

            messagebox.showinfo(
                "Winner",
                "🎉 You Won!"
            )

            reset()

        elif attempts[0] == 0:

            messagebox.showinfo(
                "Game Over",
                "😔 Game Over!\n"
                "Word: "
                + word[0]
            )

            reset()

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="GUESS",
        font=("Arial", 15, "bold"),
        bg="#27AE60",
        fg="white",
        width=15,
        command=guess_letter
    ).pack(pady=10)

    tk.Button(
        game,
        text="🔄 NEW GAME",
        font=("Arial", 14),
        bg="#E67E22",
        fg="white",
        width=15,
        command=reset
    ).pack(pady=10)

    update_word()

# BUTTON FUNCTION
# =========================================================

def create_button(
    text,
    command,
    color
):

    button = tk.Button(
        root,
        text=text,
        font=("Arial", 15, "bold"),
        width=25,
        height=1,
        bg=color,
        fg="white",
        activebackground="#FFFFFF",
        activeforeground="black",
        relief="raised",
        bd=3,
        cursor="hand2",
        command=command
    )

    button.pack(pady=7)

    return button

You said:

I want to add backgroung images in each games such as sudoku, etc

ChatGPT said:

Yes. 👍 You can give each game its own background image. Since your project is a simple Python/Tkinter project, the easiest method is to load one image inside each Toplevel game window.

For example:

Games_Project/
│
├── main.py
│
├── main_background.jpg
├── tictactoe.jpg
├── snake_ladder.jpg
├── rock_paper_scissors.jpg
├── number_guessing.jpg
└── hangman.jpg

You can also later add sudoku.jpg if you create a Sudoku game.

1. Add this helper function

Put this after creating root, before your game functions:

Python
def set_background(window, image_file, width, height):
    try:
        image = Image.open(image_file)

        image = image.resize(
            (width, height),
            Image.Resampling.LANCZOS
        )

        photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(
            image,
            master=window
        )

        background = tk.Label(
            window,
            image=photo
        )

        background.place(
            x=0,
            y=0,
            width=width,
            height=height
        )

        # VERY IMPORTANT:
        # Keep the image in memory
        window.background_photo = photo

        return background

    except FileNotFoundError:

        window.configure(
            bg="#1B2631"
        )

        print(
            "Image not found:",
            image_file
        )

        return None

This means you don't have to repeat all the image-loading code for every game.

2. Tic-Tac-Toe background

Inside tic_tac_toe(), you currently have:

Python
game.configure(bg="#1B2631")

Replace it with:

Python
set_background(
    game,
    "tictactoe.jpg",
    500,
    600
)

So the beginning becomes:

Python
def tic_tac_toe():

    game = tk.Toplevel(root)

    game.title("❌⭕ Tic-Tac-Toe")

    game.geometry("500x600")

    game.resizable(False, False)

    set_background(
        game,
        "tictactoe.jpg",
        500,
        600
    )

⚠️ One important thing

There is a small issue with putting a background directly behind your widgets.

For example, if you do:

Python
background.place(...)

and then:

Python
tk.Label(...)

the label will be placed on top of the background, which is what we want.

But if you use a Frame with a solid background:

Python
frame = tk.Frame(
    game,
    bg="#1B2631"
)

that frame can cover the background image.

For example, in Tic-Tac-Toe, change:

Python
frame = tk.Frame(
    game,
    bg="#1B2631"
)

to:

Python
frame = tk.Frame(
    game,
    bg="#1B2631"
)

This is okay if you want the board area to have a dark panel. The background will still be visible around it.
